claim: A 70% pass rate on production-derived evals is more informative than 95% on a static gold benchmark; chasing high pass rates indicates the test set is too easy to expose real failure modes.

evidence.quote: A 70% on meaningful, production-derived evals tells you more than 95% on a benchmark that doesn't reflect your users.

applies_when: production-traffic available for sampling; not applicable to pre-launch systems where synthetic eval is the only option

claim: End-to-end RAG eval lets the generator absorb retriever failures and hide them in green pass-rates; Recall@K < 0.5-0.6 is a strong signal the retriever is the bottleneck, Precision@K < 0.4 signals excessive noise into the generator.

evidence.quote: Recall@K below 0.5–0.6 is a strong signal your retriever is the bottleneck.
Precision@K below 0.4 suggests your retriever is adding too much noise.

applies_when: retriever and generator can be evaluated independently with held-out QA + gold-evidence labels

claim: Custom domain-specific trace-viewing UI yields more eval insights per engineer-hour than generic dashboards (LangSmith, Phoenix, etc.) - the highest-leverage tooling investment for an AI team improving a RAG system.

evidence.quote: The single most impactful investment I've seen AI teams make isn't a fancy evaluation dashboard – it's building a customized interface that lets anyone examine what their AI is actually doing.

applies_when: team has engineering bandwidth to build internal tools; domain-specific context matters (e.g. legal, medical, finance)

claim: For RAG generation eval, do NOT use off-the-shelf LLM-as-judge prompts; the standard process requires error analysis, prompt iteration, labeled examples, and measuring judge TPR/TNR against human annotators before estimates can be trusted.

evidence.quote: Finally, when implementing Jason's Tier 2 and 3 metrics, don't just use prompts off the shelf. The standard LLM-as-judge process requires several steps: error analysis, prompt iteration, creating labeled examples, and measuring your judge's accuracy against human labels.

applies_when: production hallucination targets near-zero; budget for human-annotation calibration phase before judge-LLM scales

claim: Cite-or-refuse contracts: if a retrieved chunk is below a confidence threshold, force refusal instead of generating an unsupported answer; this converts a known failure mode (confident hallucination) into a known refusal that the product layer can handle.

evidence.quote: If retrieval confidence is too low, the assistant refuses instead of guessing. If the user asks for private or internal data, the system refuses early.

applies_when: near-zero hallucination is a hard requirement; product can present a refusal gracefully (chat UI, not search)
